subject: PO vs Card — procurement constraints and next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: PO vs Card — procurement constraints and next steps

Hi Maya,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the time and the thoughtful questions. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Recap from today's demo:
- Goal: proof of concept for customer support summarization and routing (team: CS + Platform)
- Volume: pilot ~200k tokens/month, ramp to ~1M tokens if POC succeeds
- Success criteria: latency under 500ms for single-turn chat, cost target <$0.XX / 1k tokens (TBD)

Open procurement / commercial questions you flagged:
- Whether FintechCo can pay by credit card for an initial POC vs needing a Purchase Order (PO)
- Vendor onboarding requirements (tax W9, SOC2, vendor questionnaire)
- Interest in using a marketplace (AWS Marketplace) vs direct contract/invoice

Attachments from our side: Redwood_SOW_v1.pdf (PO language + scope) and Vendor_Onboarding_Checklist.xlsx (vendor packet).

Possible paths we typically see work well:
1) Card-first POC: credit card to stand up a short POC (30 days) to validate tech quickly, then convert to PO / reserved capacity for production.
2) PO from Day 1: provide SOW + MSA, Redwood invoices Net30 and accepts PO numbers; procurement runs onboarding in parallel.
3) Marketplace: we are listed on AWS Marketplace and can transact there, but some customers prefer direct contracting for data/terms control.

Questions for you / next steps:
- Is procurement able to approve a card payment for an initial POC, or will a PO be required from the outset?
- Who is the primary procurement contact (we can send vendor packet + W9 + SOC2 link)?
- Any mandatory vendor forms we should complete ahead of the onboarding call?

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min procurement + legal sync to walk through the packet and confirm timeline. Suggested times: Wed 10/21 11am or Thu 10/22 2pm PT.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the packet in a separate email.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

[Attachment: Redwood_SOW_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Maya Singh <maya@fintechco.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@fintechco.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO vs Card — procurement constraints and next steps

Thanks Lauren,

Appreciate the recap and the attachments. A few notes from procurement: 

- FintechCo policy is that any vendor spend above $5,000 requires a Purchase Order. For pilot spend below that threshold, procurement is sometimes OK with card, but it needs approval from our finance manager.
- Our vendor onboarding requires: completed vendor questionnaire (attached separately), signed W9, SOC2 Type II report, and bank details for ACH.
- We generally prefer direct invoicing into our AP system rather than marketplace purchases because it helps with spend reporting. Using AWS Marketplace would be allowed but it adds extra reconciliation steps and sometimes increases billing lag.

Can you confirm:
- Does Redwood support Net30 invoicing and PO numbers on invoices?
- Are you able to provide SOC2 report and a filled vendor packet quickly?
- Do you have a standard vendor code we should reference when creating the vendor in our portal?

Looping in Tom (procurement) on this thread to coordinate the vendor packet. If you can send a formal vendor packet and example invoice, we can begin vendor setup and let you know if PO will be required for the pilot.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Director, Procurement | FintechCo
maya@fintechco.com

Hi Maya / Tom,

Thanks — yes we can support the paths you outlined. Quick responses below and proposed concrete next steps: 

Answers:
- Invoicing & PO support: Redwood accepts PO numbers on invoices and offers Net30 terms by default for contract purchases. We can invoice monthly and include your PO number on each invoice.
- Documents: attaching a vendor packet and our onboarding checklist (Vendor_Onboarding_Checklist.xlsx). Our SOC2 Type II report is available here: https://console.redwood.ai/soc2/2026 (we can provide the PDF under an NDA if required). W9 attached to the packet.
- Vendor code: we do not currently have a pre-provisioned vendor code for FintechCo; once you create the vendor profile in your portal, share the internal vendor ID and we'll reference it on invoices.

Recommended next steps:
1) We will send the completed vendor packet and a sample invoice by end of day (attached).
2) If FintechCo prefers a rapid technical validation, start the POC on card for initial spend under $5k, then convert to PO for production. If procurement requires PO from day 1, we are ready to sign the SOW and invoice on Net30.
3) Schedule a 30-min onboarding call (procurement + legal + finance) to confirm checklist items and timeline. Suggested: Fri 10/23 9am PT or Wed 10/28 11am PT.

Links & references: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/DEAL-2026-145

I attached: Vendor_Onboarding_Checklist.xlsx and a sample invoice. Please let me know the best time for the onboarding call and whether you want us to start the POC on card while vendor setup proceeds.

Best,

Lauren / Maya,

Received the vendor packet and the sample invoice — thanks. We'll kick off vendor onboarding in our portal today. A couple items from AP:
- Please send a formal invoice (PDF) for the initial amount you expect to bill (even if the customer will pay by card) so we have the record to create the vendor.
- Once the vendor is created, we will provide the vendor ID and advise if a PO is required for the pilot. If the pilot spend is below $5k, we typically approve card payment and then create a PO for subsequent invoices.
- Can you provide a copy of your bank details for ACH payments (we will store this behind our secure portal)?

I'm available for a short call Wed 10/28 11am PT to walk through the onboarding checklist.
